sentences.text:
Vide order dated 07.02.2017, interim protection was granted, which reads as follows:-
"Heard learned counsel for the applicants and learned A.G.A. for the State.

The present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed for quashing the charge sheet dated 15.01.2016 arising out of Case Crime No. 170 of 2015 under Sections 323, 406, 498A I.P.C., and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Shikarpur, District Bulandshahr.

It is contended by learned counsel for the applicants that earlier, the applicants had filed criminal revision no.2894 of 2016 in which the matter was referred to mediation centre of this Court vide order dated 22.09.2016, copy of which is annexed as Annexure-3 to the affidavit accompanying the present 482 Cr.P.C. application.

Learned counsel further contends that the mediation between the parties has been successful vide settlement agreement dated 19.01.2017, copy of which is annexed as Annexure-5 to the affidavit accompanying the 482 Cr.P.C.
It is thus contended that initiation of the present proceedings is bad in law.
Issue notice to the opposite party no.2 returnable within a period of four weeks.
Steps be taken within a week.
Learned A.G.A. prays for and is granted four weeks' time to file counter affidavit.
Opposite party no.2 may also file counter affidavit within the same period.
As prayed by learned counsel for the applicants two weeks' thereafter, is granted for filing rejoinder affidavit.
List immediately after expiry of the aforesaid period before appropriate Court.

Till the next date of listing, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicants in the aforesaid case."
4.

Learned counsel for applicants has also drawn attention to order dated 11.03.2022 passed in Criminal Revision No.2894 of 2016, Prabhat Bhooshan & 3 others v. State of U.P. & another indicating the fact that parties have entered into compromise in mediation proceedings before this Court indicating that the mediation was successful.

sentences.text: The mediation report was also indicated in the order and order impugned in the Criminal Revision passed in Criminal Case No.267 of 2014 was quashed.

5. A perusal of counter affidavit filed on behalf of opposite party no.2 indicates that in paragraph 5 onward, opposite party no.2 has admitted that their dispute was referred before Mediation and conciliation Centre of this court vide order dated 22.09.2016 passed in Criminal Revision no.2894 of 2016 and settlement has been arrived at which was implemented and due to which opposite party no.2 does not want to proceed with criminal proceedings.

State of Gujarat and another, reported in (2017) 9 SCC 641 has indicated the aspects under which this Court exercising powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C. can quash proceedings on account of compromise having been effected between the parties.
